root_cause.text: The error handling path in `pvrdma_alloc_ucontext()` explicitly calls `pvrdma_uar_free()` to free the User Address Register (UAR), but then immediately calls `pvrdma_dealloc_ucontext()` which also frees the same UAR resource, resulting in a double free of the same memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the explicit `pvrdma_uar_free(vdev, &context->uar);` call from the error path and replaces it with a comment stating "pvrdma_dealloc_ucontext() also frees the UAR", confirming that `pvrdma_dealloc_ucontext()` already handles UAR cleanup. The vulnerability exists because the original code at line 325 calls `pvrdma_uar_free()` before delegating to `pvrdma_dealloc_ucontext()` at line 326, causing the same resource to be freed twice.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable code is present in the `pvrdma_alloc_ucontext()` function. At lines 330-334, when `ib_copy_to_udata()` fails, the error handling path explicitly calls `pvrdma_uar_free(vdev, &context->uar)` to free the UAR. However, immediately after on line 336, it calls `pvrdma_dealloc_ucontext(&context->ibucontext)`, which internally calls `pvrdma_uar_free()` again at line 365 in the `pvrdma_dealloc_ucontext()` function. This results in a double-free of the same UAR resource. The fix would be to remove the explicit `pvrdma_uar_free()` call at line 331 since `pvrdma_dealloc_ucontext()` already handles UAR deallocation.
